extracted.intended_audience: economists, patent analysts, policymakers, and researchers evaluating patent value
extracted.subtask_description: Use forward citation patterns (counts, growth, citer diversity, and cohort rank) as empirical indicators of patent quality and social value, applying cohort normalization and time lags. Intended to assess issued patents (preferably 5+ years post-grant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward citations as foundational quality indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Forward (future) patent citations correlate with independent measures of social welfare in a technology (Trajtenberg finds citation-weighted patent counts correlate with CT-scanner welfare at r ≈ 0.75).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forward citation measures as a primary indicator of patent value rather than raw patent counts; treat them as credible signals of technological influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation-weighted patent counts (nonlinear informativeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The marginal informativeness of citations increases with citation count: high-citation patents are disproportionately valuable (a patent with 50 citations can be more than 50× as valuable as one with a single citation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply nonlinear weighting when aggregating citation counts (e.g., give far greater weight to top-cited patents) because value is concentrated in the citation tail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort normalization (technology class + grant year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation patterns vary by field and over time; raw counts must be normalized within a technology class and grant-year cohort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare a patent's citations to its cohort (same technology class and grant year) to obtain meaningful percentile ranks or normalized scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation lag — require multi-year window (5+ years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citational impact accumulates over time; meaningful quality assessment requires sufficient post-grant time (Trajtenberg and others note a citation lag).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay quality judgments until at least ~5 years after grant (use citation windows such as years 0–5 vs 5–10 to observe growth or acceleration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pioneer quality marker — far-above-cohort citations (top decile/percentile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pioneering foundational patents have forward citations far exceeding the cohort median — frequently in the top decile or top percentiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat top-decile/percentile patents as the primary value-bearing patents in a technology; identify such patents as likely foundational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pioneer quality marker — cross-technology citing (high generality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundational patents are cited by patents across multiple technology classes (high generality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High generality (citations from many classes) is evidence the patent influenced multiple technological domains and increases confidence in high value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pioneer quality marker — cited by major industry incumbents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents cited by major incumbent firms indicate industry recognition and commercial significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of citations from large incumbents strengthens the claim that a patent is influential and valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement-patent markers (within-field incremental value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvement patents typically have forward citations at or above the cohort median, receive citations mainly from the same technology class, and show steady citation accumulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret median-or-above within-class citations and steady accrual as indicators of useful but more incremental, within-field value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-quality markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Signals of low value include zero forward citations 5+ years post-grant, citations restricted to the inventor's own firm (self-citations only), or citations only from minor entities (no major-firm validation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these markers as reliable indicators of likely low social value; treat patents with such patterns as weak candidates for high valuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation diversity — diversity of citers across firms and art units
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality inference is strengthened when citations come from a diverse set of firms and patent examiners/art units rather than a narrow set of sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the mix of citing entities (multiple independent firms, different art units) to increase confidence in the citation signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation acceleration pattern (growth trajectory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation growth pattern — accelerating, steady, or decelerating — provides information about how influence evolves (e.g., pioneers accumulate citations over decades; improvement patents show steadier rates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare citation counts in earlier vs later windows (e.g., years 0–5 vs 5–10); accelerating patterns signal rising influence and higher expected value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of citations as signal mechanisms (examiner, applicant, litigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different kinds of citations carry different informational content: examiner citations indicate relevance found by examiners, applicant citations (IDS) indicate applicants deem the prior art material, and litigation citations signal commercial importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate citation sources when possible: litigation citations and examiner citations may warrant greater weight as indicators of material influence; applicant citations also convey technological awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and caveats in interpreting citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Caveats include variation in examiner citation practices across art units and time, citation lag, defensive citations that inflate counts, and strategic non-citation that can deflate counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust interpretation for institutional and strategic factors; do not rely solely on raw citation counts without considering these distortions and corroborating evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative percentile thresholds for quality signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical thresholds for patents 5+ years post-grant: forward citations ≥ 75th cohort percentile = strong quality signal; 25th–75th = ambiguous (combine with other indicators); ≤ 25th = weak; zero citations = very weak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these percentile bands as a pragmatic decision rule when evaluating individual patents, but complement with other indicators for ambiguous cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical validation by subsequent studies (corroborating evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent research corroborates the citation-quality link (e.g., Hall, Jaffe & Trajtenberg 2005: ~3% firm market value per citation; Lanjouw & Schankerman 2004: citations dominate quality indicators; Bessen 2008: correlation with renewal patterns; OECD adoption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these external validations as supporting evidence for using citations as a primary quality metric, and consult them when calibrating weighting schemes or interpreting magnitudes.
